paragraphs: SirsiDynix sells software for libraries, starting with library automation and the modules its products page lists for acquisition, cataloging, and circulation. A second line is discovery, which the products page says lets patrons find the library, search for materials and services, and reserve or check out those materials. Named library systems include Symphony, Horizon, and EOS.Web, which the page describes as an integrated library system built for special libraries.

Modules named on the same page include BLUEcloud Acquisitions, Analytics, Cataloging, Circulation, Commerce, and Serials, with BLUEcloud Mobile2 putting the catalog in a patron app. Staff tools include MobileStaff for circulation away from the desk and SymphonyWeb, which the page presents as the Symphony client in a browser.

The products page sorts these offerings by library type: public, academic, K-12, consortia, and special libraries. Case studies name users such as Los Angeles County Library System, Cecil County Public Library, and Brigham Young University. One case study names the U.S. Department of Commerce, and another names the Wyoming State Public Library.
